classification.difficultyReason: Recover the central angle from arc length, calculate sector and triangle areas, then recognise and subtract those regions to obtain the shaded segment; the preceding parts scaffold the final connection.

content.prompt: The diagram below shows an arc $PQ$ of length $40$ cm, subtended by some angle in a circle with radius $70$ cm. Find

spec.description: Schematic circle with centre O, lower horizontal chord PQ, two single-ticked radii and the 40 cm label beneath the minor arc. Light blue identifies the requested minor segment; no angle value is supplied in the diagram.
spec.mathematics: OP = OQ = 70 cm; the minor arc PQ has length 40 cm. The drawing is schematic and its pictured central angle is not a numerical given.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; no calculated angle, area or chord length.

children.label: c
children.prompt: the area of $\triangle POQ$, to the nearest $\text{cm}^2$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: the shaded area correct to the nearest $\text{cm}^2$.

answer.worked:
The shaded segment is the sector less the triangle. Use the unrounded triangle area.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{segment}}&=A_{\text{sector}}-A_{\triangle POQ}\\A_{\text{segment}}&=1400-2450\sin\left(\frac{4}{7}\right)\\A_{\text{segment}}&\approx75\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
